summary: Pre-Vote update required a model change. Reference, MC, Trace and Update suites were updated and two prior-model defects repaired; the rebased harness produced 19 fresh traces that all replay. Model checking found two update-introduced defects in the Pre-Vote round lifecycle, both reproduced at engine and runtime level: a round started while Candidate survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect (MC-1), and the Pre-Vote-triggered election skips the voter check after a leader removes itself (MC-2).
validation_limits: All model checking is bounded (3 servers, MaxTerm 2, MaxLogIndex 4, bounded elections, membership changes, crashes, drops and messages); several BFS runs stopped at their time limit with states left on the queue.
The runtime election tick (lease expiry, Pre-Vote mode, round rate limit) is not traced; engine-level traces call pre_elect/elect directly and RunCommands emulates the runtime command boundary.
The runtime reproduction uses the public trigger().elect(true) path; the purely timer-driven path is shown by the model counterexample and the engine-level test, not by a deterministic cluster test.
No liveness or fairness property is checked.
The specula ci-result command is not installed in this environment, so the generated CI reports were not produced.

findings.title: Stale Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect
findings.cause: establish_leader consumes only the candidate and become_leader does not clear pre_candidate, so a Pre-Vote round started by the election tick (or trigger().elect(true)) while the node was still a Candidate survives; RaftCore still delivers its responses and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on quorum.
findings.trigger: A Candidate's election timer fires (or trigger().elect(true) is called) while its real election is in flight; the delayed vote response makes it leader; then a peer's granting Pre-Vote response for the earlier probe arrives.
findings.consequence: The freshly established leader increments its term and becomes Candidate while keeping its Leader object; followers holding its lease reject the new vote request, leaving the cluster without a working leader for at least a lease period; debug builds panic on the leader.vote >= state.vote assertion (writes fail with Fatal(Panicked)); after self-removal the stale grant makes a non-voter start an election.

premises: The election tick and ExternalCommand::Elect{pre_vote:true} do not check for an in-flight candidate before pre_elect().
establish_leader/become_leader leave pre_candidate set and the PreVoteResponse filter checks only pre_candidate presence and leader id.
Pre-Vote is enabled by Config::enable_pre_vote, the runtime toggle, or a per-call trigger().elect(true).

findings.title: Pre-Vote-triggered election skips the voter check, so a leader that removed itself starts an election
findings.cause: handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on quorum without re-checking is_voter, and nothing cancels a Pre-Vote round when the leader removes itself; ExternalCommand::Elect{pre_vote:true} accepts a leader and checks is_voter only at round start.
findings.trigger: Operator calls trigger().elect(true) on the leader while follower leases have expired; the leader removes itself with change_membership (removed_leader_step_down = Never or within the After window); a delayed granting Pre-Vote response arrives.
findings.consequence: The removed, non-voter node persists an inflated term and sends RequestVote at that term to the new configuration (observed term 1 -> 2 on the removed node), the disruption Pre-Vote is meant to prevent.

premises: The Pre-Vote-triggered elect() has no voter check while the tick and external elect paths check is_voter.
A leader keeps leading after self-removal under removed_leader_step_down = Never or until the After(ms) countdown.
trigger().elect(true) is accepted on a leader.
